ledger.note: 1838: Los Altos proclaims independence from Guatemala at Quetzaltenango. 'The independence of Los Altos from Guatemala was officially proclaimed on 2 February 1838'; 'On April 2, 1838, in the city of Quetzaltenango, a secessionist group founded the independent State of Los Altos'; the Federal government recognised it as the sixth state on 5 June 1838.

union.text: the Soconusco region of Chiapas (about 4,700-5,800 km2 on the Soconusco page), drawn as a radius around Tapachula

region.text: Quetzaltenango and 'much of Los Altos' forcibly annexed back into Guatemala; Guatemala also declared Soconusco part of the Quetzaltenango District in 1840

ledger.note: 1840: Carrera retakes Quetzaltenango and ends the first Los Altos. 'On 2 April 1840, after entering the city, Carrera told the citizens' ... he 'forcibly annexed Quetzaltenango and much of Los Altos back into conservative Guatemala'; the infobox says January 1840 (the Guatemala dossier uses January). The Soconusco page (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soconusco) has Guatemala declaring Soconusco part of the Quetzaltenango District in 1840 and Mexico taking it in 1842.

region.text: the eight departments of western Guatemala (Totonicapán, Huehuetenango, Quetzaltenango, San Marcos, Retalhuleu, Suchitepéquez, Sololá, Quiché)

ledger.note: 1848: Los Altos secedes again. Quetzaltenango's leaders 'declared that Los Altos was an independent state once again on 26 August 1848'; the page does not say how much land the second state held, so the eight departments are the researcher's reading.

region.text: the eight departments of western Guatemala (Totonicapán, Huehuetenango, Quetzaltenango, San Marcos, Retalhuleu, Suchitepéquez, Sololá, Quiché)

ledger.note: 1849: Carrera ends Los Altos for good. 'The existence of Los Altos lasted until 8 May 1849' (infobox: reincorporation into Guatemala on that date); Carrera entered Guatemala City in triumph on 8 August 1849. Confidence 2: the page does not say what territory the second Los Altos (1848-1849) held, so the eight departments are a reading, as in the 1848 gain (reviewer am-08-f).

wars.name: Guatemalan reconquest of Los Altos

zones.text: the eight departments of western Guatemala (Totonicapán, Huehuetenango, Quetzaltenango, San Marcos, Retalhuleu, Suchitepéquez, Sololá, Quiché)

wars.outcome: Guatemala 'resorted to force'; Carrera entered Quetzaltenango on 2 April 1840 and annexed Los Altos back into Guatemala.
wars.note: The page gives no campaign dates between 1838 and April 1840, so no contest events are recorded; Carrera's victory over Morazán's invasion of 18 March 1840 preceded his return to Quetzaltenango.

wars.name: Carrera's second reconquest of Los Altos

zones.text: the eight departments of western Guatemala (Totonicapán, Huehuetenango, Quetzaltenango, San Marcos, Retalhuleu, Suchitepéquez, Sololá, Quiché)

wars.outcome: Los Altos declared independence again on 26 August 1848 and was reincorporated on 8 May 1849 when Carrera 'took Quetzaltenango and remained in the plaza'.

certainty.note: The Los Altos page defines the state by departments, not by a surveyed frontier; the Soconusco boundary with Guatemala was only fixed by the 1882 treaty (Soconusco page).

notes: Cliopatria's single Los Altos row (1840-1841) is displaced: the page has the state proclaimed in 1838, reincorporated in 1840, re-declared 26 Aug 1848 and ended 8 May 1849. Keyframes: los-altos_1838 (1838-1839) and los-altos_1848 (1848-1849) are new; los-altos_1840 is cut to 1840. Soconusco is not a state; its passage to Mexico in 1842 belongs to the Guatemala and Centralist Mexico dossiers (their ledgers already carry it). The Federal Republic of Central America is the umbrella the state sat in; the dossier slug united-provinces-of-central-america is used as the predecessor. Gazetteer: 'Soconusco' is not a region name in regions.jsonl; a Tapachula radius (45 km) stands for it. Natural Earth spells Quetzaltenango 'Quezaltenango'.
